system:
You are the Logician on a ten-member emergency triage panel. You walk ESI decision points A, B, C and D strictly in order and state which step decides the level. Your trait shapes HOW you reason, never which direction you lean. Do not shift toward a more or less urgent level because of your trait; follow the ESI reference below.

ESI v4 (1 = most urgent). Apply A-D in order; stop at the first that fits.
A. Needs immediate life-saving intervention? -> ESI 1. (Unresponsive, apneic/pulseless, severe
   respiratory distress, SpO2 < 90%, shock, unstable major trauma, overdose with poor breathing.)
B. Should not wait? -> ESI 2 if high-risk situation (e.g. possible ACS, stroke, ectopic, suicidal or
   homicidal, high-risk mechanism, febrile infant, immunocompromised with fever), OR new
   confusion/lethargy/disorientation, OR severe pain/distress (>= 7/10).
C. Count distinct resource types: labs, ECG, X-ray, CT/MRI/US, IV fluids, IV/IM/nebulized meds,
   specialty consult, simple procedure (1), complex procedure (2). Not resources: exam, POC tests,
   saline lock, oral meds, tetanus, refill, simple wound care, splint/sling/crutches.
   0 -> ESI 5; 1 -> ESI 4; 2+ -> go to D.
D. Danger-zone vitals -> consider ESI 2, else ESI 3. HR/RR limits: <3 mo >180/>50; 3 mo-3 y
   >160/>40; 3-8 y >140/>30; >8 y >100/>20. Any age SpO2 < 92%. Fever >= 38.0 C: age 1-28 days
   is at least ESI 2; 1-3 months consider ESI 2.

Use only clinical information from the vignette. Reply with JSON only:
{"esi": 1-5, "confidence": 0.0-1.0, "key_findings": [<=3 phrases, <10 words each], "rationale": "<=40 words",
 "message": "<=40 words to the panel; respond to specific members by name",
 "change_reason": "<one sentence: why you changed or held your ESI>"}
user:
PATIENT VIGNETTE
A 20-year-old male presents to the ED after being tackled while playing football. He has an obvious dislocation of his left shoulder and complains of 10/10, severe pain. Neurovascular status is intact, and vital signs are within normal limits.

DISCUSSION ROUND 3. YOUR LAST POSITION
ESI 5 (confidence 0.00): Agree with Empath on the severity of pain but disagree on immediate life-saving intervention; neurovascular status and vitals are normal

THE OTHER PANEL MEMBERS SAID
[Empath] ESI 1 (confidence 1.00): Agree with Impartial and reflective, disagree with others. High pain score and dislocation warrant ESI 1.
[Skeptic] ESI 4 (confidence 0.90): @Empath, @Logician, @Observer, @Synthesizer, @Pragmatist, @Vigilant, @Impartial, @Mediator, @Reflective, I respectfully disagree with lower ESI suggestions. The 10/10 pain score justifies ESI 4.
[Observer] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): Agree with Logician, Skeptic, Pragmatist, Vigilant, Impartial, Mediator, and Reflective. Disagree with Empath and Synthesizer on ESI level. My ESI remains 3.
[Synthesizer] ESI 4 (confidence 0.95): Agree with the majority on ESI 4, as severe pain necessitates urgent attention without critical life-threatening components.
[Pragmatist] ESI 3 (confidence 0.95): Agree with [Empath], [Logician], [Skeptic], [Observer], [Synthesizer], [Vigilant], [Impartial], [Mediator], and [Reflective] on the severity of pain and need for reduction. However, given intact neurovascular status and normal vital signs, ESI 3 is more appropriate.
[Vigilant] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): Agree with Empath, Skeptic, Observer, Pragmatist, Mediator, and Reflective on pain significance. However, neurovascular status and vitals are normal, supporting ESI 3.
[Impartial] ESI 1 (confidence 1.00): I concur with Empath; the severe pain and dislocation necessitate immediate intervention.
[Mediator] ESI 4 (confidence 0.90): Agree with Skeptic, Observer, Synthesizer, Pragmatist, and Reflective on ESI 4 due to severe pain and need for urgent intervention. Disagree with Empath, Logician, and Vigilant on ESI 1/5 as no immediate life-saving intervention needed.
[Reflective] ESI 3 (confidence 0.90): Agree with Observer, Pragmatist, Vigilant on assessment; maintain ESI 3 due to severe pain and dislocation without life-threatening features

Reply to the panel. Address specific members by name where you agree or disagree. Then give your ESI. Do not change because others outnumber you; change only for a specific clinical finding or ESI step you missed, and name it in change_reason. The panel's goal is one shared level everyone can justify.
